text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Iraqi press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Tunisia donates medicine to Iraqi children.
- The U.N. sanctions committee on Iraq rejects Iraqi agricultural purchases under the oil-for-food deal.
- Iraq asks the U.N. to use a border post between Iraq and Syria to handle Iraq's imports of goods under the oil deal.
- An editorial lashing out at U.N. arms inspectors.
(The above except the editorial were carried by IRAQ and THAWRA)
- National Assembly continues its discussions on the implementation of the oil deal.
- An editorial urges the U.N. Security Council to end sanctions on Iraq and blaming the U.S. for prolonging them.
- A commentary critisised Arab leaders for not adopting firm stand against the U.S. House of Representatives decision to move American embassy from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem.
- BABEL (Owned by President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday)
- Editorial condemning visit of U.S. Secretary of Defence to the Middle East visit.
